_comment: Numbers the page renders. Upload a new copy of this file and the page
updates — no HTML change, no redeploy of anything else.
`decode` is a best recorded rate on that machine, or null for 'not
measured'. Null renders as 'not measured' rather than a blank or a zero,
because a missing measurement and a slow one are different claims.
`modes` is how the model runs there: gpu = fully resident, ssd = experts
stream from disk, hyb = split CPU/GPU. Several modes means the app can
use any of them; an empty list renders 'does not fit'.
`os` and `backend` drive the two tab rows. os is mac|linux; backend is
metal|cuda|rocm|cann. Choosing an OS disables the backends that cannot run
on it, and the machine, post and download lists all filter to the pair.
A backend with no machine yet (cann) still renders a tab, disabled, because
'no measurement yet' and 'not supported' are different claims.
_provenance: The M4 mini and DGX Spark rows were measured directly on those machines in August 2026 and carry the method in their notes. On 12 August 2026 three M1 Ultra rows were re-measured the same way and now carry medians with spreads: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Laguna-S-2.1 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Where a re-measurement moved a number it is recorded here rather than silently overwritten: Laguna-S-2.1 30.8 -> 33.4 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash 27.5 -> 28.0 (both faster than published), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 73.7 -> 72.3. The M1 Ultra DeepSeek-V4-Flash size was corrected from 97.6 GB to 87 GB: the old figure matched no file on the machine and disagreed with the same model's own M2 Max and DGX Spark rows. A fourth attempt, M2 Max Qwen3-4B, was WITHDRAWN rather than published: two runs of the identical script disagreed by 1.7x, so that row is now null. TWO LIMITS THIS EXERCISE EXPOSED, which apply to every row on this page. First, decode is not a single rate: measured on M2 Max, the 1->129 token slope and the 129->513 slope differ by 15%, because attention costs more as the context grows -- so any figure here depends on the token count it was taken at, which is 129. Second, these machines are shared, and a busy machine can halve the number; spreads are quoted so a reader can see when that happened. The remaining M1 Ultra and M2 Max rows are still carried over verbatim from the first version of this page and have NOT been re-verified. Prices are approximate street or list prices in August 2026, recorded so a rate can be read against what the machine costs -- they move, and they are not quotes. Muse Glimmer 30B was ADDED to the M1 Ultra and M2 Max boxes after the 12 August exercise and does not share its method: both figures are llama.cpp's llama-bench tg128 (build b10360, r=3, 12 August 2026), an instrument reporting a mean over repetitions rather than the median-of-paired-estimates used elsewhere here, so the two rows are comparable with each other but not strictly with their neighbours, and the notes say so. Where two runs exist the LOWER is published: M2 Max decode 6.42 and 6.25 -> 6.3, prefill 82.65 and 76.75 -> 78. Two figures also exist for the M1 Ultra and both are kept rather than one being chosen silently: tg128 23.20 and tg64 ~28.9. tg128 is published because the rest of the column is quoted at 129 generated tokens; the tg64 figure is not wrong, it is a shorter generation, which this page already records as producing a higher rate. The tg64 run is documented as having a ds4 Q4_K kernel substitution active and the tg128 runs do not say, which is why these rows decline to name an engine's kernels the way their neighbours do. These are also the only two rows on this page measured on TWO machines by one instrument, and the 0.28x ratio between them against a 0.605 tier prediction is the reason no rate here is scaled from another machine's. In late August 2026 a fifth box was added: an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), running the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash file as the DGX Spark row through the ROCm reference engine, at 15.0 tok/s decode. It is published at the machine's default power governor rather than at its best observed setting, because the default is what a buyer gets; forcing the GPU to `high` is worth +0.8% on decode and +6.7% on prefill, and up to +26% when the CPU is also busy, but it costs a co-running CPU job about 40% and was still showing 104C peaks after 25 minutes of soak, so it is not a free setting and is not what the row reports. The machine's NPU is excluded from the figure for the plainer reason that it was measured and is worth +0.4%. The Ryzen row's price is what was actually paid for the machine (£3,099, Bosgame M5, August 2026) rather than a list price, which is why it is the only row in a currency other than dollars; it has not been converted, because a made-up exchange rate is not better provenance than none. On 29 August 2026 two rows were added to the M1 Ultra table, each measured on that machine: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at 30.8 tok/s and GLM-5.3-Flash at 24.1 tok/s. The GLM-5.2 row (3.5 tok/s, SSD-streamed) was removed rather than re-measured, because the model is no longer offered; its number was not superseded by a new measurement of the same model and is not claimed to be wrong.

boxes.label: M1 Ultra · 64-core GPU · 128 GB
boxes.price: from $3,999 at launch · discontinued, used market
boxes.note: Three of these six rows were re-measured on this machine on 12 August 2026; the figure is the median of paired estimates, not a best-ever run. Decode is isolated as the difference between a 129-token and a 1-token completion so prefill is excluded, and repetitions alternate A/B/B/A so drift lands on both arms. Each model runs on the engine the app picks for it, and they are not the same engine: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on llama.cpp with the ds4 kernels — 72.3, ten estimates spanning 67.5–78.0; Laguna-S-2.1 on the ds4 reference engine — 33.4, eight estimates spanning 33.1–34.3; DeepSeek-V4-Flash on our own Rust/Metal engine — 28.0, eight estimates spanning 27.8–28.2. The machine was shared with other work throughout, which is why the Qwen3.6 spread is the wide one; the DeepSeek figure independently reproduces a 27.9–28.2 anchor measured by a different harness. The last two rows are out-of-core rates and are still carried over unverified: GLM-5.2 is not present on this machine at all, and Kimi-K3 is present but its streaming mode is the untested claim — one attempt at an out-of-core model of that class drove the machine into 42 GB of swap and was stopped. Muse Glimmer 30B is measured by a different instrument and is marked so rather than blended in: llama.cpp's own llama-bench, build b10360, on 12 August 2026 — tg128 23.20 ± 0.19 over three repetitions, with a pp512 prefill of 247.55 ± 0.87. That is a mean over repetitions, not the median of paired estimates the rows above use. It is quoted at 128 generated tokens because that is nearest the 129 the rest of the column uses; the same model on this machine was separately recorded at ~28.9 tok/s on tg64, and that gap between 64 and 128 tokens is the context effect described below, not a contradiction. llama.cpp is the only engine that can load this architecture — our own engine has no path for it — but which of the two Q4_K matvec paths that run used is not recorded, so unlike the rows above this one names no kernels. Two rows were added on 29 August 2026 and both were measured on this machine. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — 30.8, the median of three llama-bench tg128 repetitions (30.78 ± 0.03), running on llama.cpp; its prefill is 560.7 tok/s at pp512. GLM-5.3-Flash — 24.1, on the ds4 reference engine, fully GPU-resident at 32K context; the same model measures 17.6 at a 9,600-token prompt, so the headline is a short-context figure like the others on this table and long sessions are slower. GLM-5.2 has been removed from this row. It never fit in memory on a 128 GB machine — 216.7 GB, streamed from SSD — and GLM-5.3-Flash now runs resident on the same hardware at roughly seven times the rate, so the older model is no longer offered.

boxes.label: M2 Max · 64 GB
boxes.note: The same catalogue, scored for 64 GB. Qwen3-4B was measured twice here on 12 August 2026 and the two runs disagreed by 1.7× — 43.4 tok/s and then 74.9 tok/s from the identical script, model and engine. The first run was taken minutes after a 2.3 GB file landed on the machine, so the machine's state rather than the model dominated it. The row is therefore withdrawn rather than published at either figure: a number that does not mean what it says is worse than an admitted gap. It will return when it can be measured on a quiescent machine. The other three rows are still carried over from the first version of this page and have not been re-verified — this machine currently has 27 GB of disk free, so the 22 GB Qwen3.6 and the 48 GB Laguna-S cannot be stored without freeing space, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 87 GB is out-of-core here, which is what the 2.9 would cost. Muse Glimmer 30B was measured on both this machine and the M1 Ultra, by the same llama-bench instrument and in the same window — tg128 6.42 ± 0.08, and 6.25 ± 0.25 on a re-run, published at the lower 6.3; prefill 82.65 and 76.75 on the two runs, so ~78. The point of measuring it twice is what it says about every unmeasured row on this page: this machine delivers 0.28× the Ultra's rate, where scaling by GPU tier would have predicted 0.605 and advertised ~14 tok/s to a Mac that gives ~6.3. A control model measured on both boxes in the same window ran 3.0× slower here too, so this is the machine and not something peculiar to Muse Glimmer. This is also the smallest M2 Max — 30 of a possible 38 GPU cores — so a fuller Max should beat it.

boxes.label: M4 mini · 16 GB
boxes.note: A 16 GB machine is offered the models that suit it, not the whole catalogue. Both rows were re-measured on this machine in August 2026, decode isolated as the difference between a 129-token and a 1-token completion so that prefill is excluded. The larger Qwen3 variants are absent because they cannot be tested here rather than because they are slow: 14B needs a download this machine has no room for, and 32B is a 20 GB file on a 16 GB machine with 12.7 GB free — it cannot be stored, let alone run.

boxes.label: DGX Spark · GB10 · 128 GB
boxes.note: Not a Local Mind machine — the app is macOS only. This is the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash file on an NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell desktop through the reference CUDA engine, so the model and the quantisation are comparable to the Mac rows even though the engine is not. Measured August 2026 as an A/B/B/A sequence, three repetitions per arm, GPU clock sampled throughout (2405–2535 MHz); the repetitions spanned 0.06 tok/s. The weights sit in unified memory rather than streaming, which is why an 87 GB model reports a resident rate on a 128 GB box.

boxes.label: Bosgame M5 · Ryzen AI Max+ 395 · 128 GB
boxes.note: Not a Local Mind machine — the app is macOS only. This is the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash file as the DGX Spark row, 86.7 GB on disk, on a Bosgame M5 mini-PC (AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 “Strix Halo”, Radeon 8060S, 128 GB LPDDR5X, 2 TB SSD) through the reference ROCm engine, so the model and the quantisation are comparable to the Mac rows even though the engine is not. Measured August 2026 at a 2048-token context; eight baseline repetitions spanned 0.03 tok/s (15.00–15.03) and the GPU clock was sampled throughout (1707 MHz mean). The weights sit in unified memory rather than streaming, which is why an 87 GB model reports a resident rate on a 128 GB box. The price is what was paid, not a list figure, and it is worth reading beside the DGX Spark row rather than instead of it: this machine is the cheaper of the two and the slower of the two on this model. Two things specific to it are worth stating rather than hiding. The rate depends on the GPU power governor: this figure is the out-of-the-box auto setting, and forcing high moves decode to 15.1 and prefill by 6.7% — a setting, not a property of the silicon. And its XDNA2 NPU, which no other box here has, was measured co-executing the output projection: it is worth +0.4%, so it is not used for this number. The 126 TOPS on the box is the platform total across NPU, GPU and CPU; the NPU's own share of it is 50.
